title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of Member States to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
In 2022-23, five municipalities including [AYAH TO ADD] adapted green local resource-based methodologies to implement climate adaptation measures. The government improved its technical capacities on green local resource-based methodologies which tackles fragility drivers including climate change.
The government generated 20,000 green working days which has significantly contributed to the creation of greater socio-economic opportunities through strengthened employability, access, to income and jobs and empowerment.
In 2022-23, the Government of Jordan created more than 1 million working days for Syrian refugees and host communities and supported nonprofit organizations in implementing Employment Intensive Investment Programmes including with the Ministry of Local Administration, the Mininstry of Public Works, and the Ministry of Agriculture, which contributed to enhancing basic services and infrastructure in more than 40 municipalities in Jordan. With the support of the European Union, UNESCO, Italy, the World Bank, and the Ministry of Local Administration, the ILO supported the municipalities to enable them to apply climate change adaptation measures based on the community needs.
The ILO also developed the capacity of the Ministry of Local Adminstration and its affiliate entitites (municipalities) in the geen local resource methodologies to enhance their technicial, manegarial and financial capacities including the training of 60 engineers to implement, oversee and monitor employment intensive investment programmes. Finally, the ILO supported the aforementioned entities in the development of monitoring frameworks and reporting mechanisms for the employment generation indicators.
VIa the support of the European Union, Government of Italy, the World Bank, and the Government of Germany, and in collaboration with UNESCO, the Ministry of Local Administration, and the KFW Development Bank, the ILO supported the Govrnment with expertise and facilitated the implementation of the employment intensive investment programmes and a rigorous capacity-building programme.

description.narrative: In March 2022, the Ministry of Youth launched the green job search clubs to increase employment of young people in the green economy, a measure which will promote just transition in Jordan by tackling the issue of youth unemployment and under-emplyoment in the country. With the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the Ministry of Youth in the establishment of green job search clubs and in the delivery of capacity-building for 120 members of its staff and their certification as master trainers.

Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative: In October 2022, the Ministry of Youth incorporated the Job Search Clubs in the National Youth Strategy and the corresponding implementation plan in Jordan. These clubs are acknolwedged as a main vehicle that can support improved employment outcomes for young people in Jordan. With the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands and the Regional Development and Protection Programme, the ILO produced five research papers to assess the youth employment challenges in Jordan both from a supply and demand perspectives and taking into account the implications of the trends on employment. These papers were launched after extensive discussions with the constituents and aim at instituting policy reforms and include the following: 1) The Potential Role of Exports in Promoting Formalization and Decent Job Creation for Youth in Jordan 2) Growth, Macroeconomic Policies and Employment: The impact of macroeconomic and trade policies on employment generation in Jordan 3) Platform work in Jordan: Challenges and opportunities 4) School-to-work transition of young women and men in Jordan 5) Skills for Green and Digital Transitions and Employment in Jordan
